svg.title: YOLOv8s clone architecture as implemented in baseline/yolov8sclone
svg.desc: CSPDarknet backbone with C2f blocks, PAN-FPN neck, and an anchor-free decoupled head with Distribution Focal Loss. Shapes are for a 640x640 input and 2 classes. Module numbers follow the published YOLOv8 layout.
svg.text: 11.136 M parameters at 2 classes (backbone 5.08 M · neck 3.94 M · Detect 2.12 M). Module numbers follow the published YOLOv8 layout. Shapes are C×H×W for a 640×640 input.
Input
12 C2f
10 Upsample ×2
11 Concat 768 ch
13 Upsample ×2
14 Concat 384 ch
17 Concat 384 ch
20 Concat 768 ch (skip from P5)
66 = 4 × 16 DFL bins + 2 classes
decode
8400 anchor points
C2f — YOLOv8's CSP block (replaces YOLOv5's C3)
Conv1×1 splits the input into two halves of c channels.
One half is chained through n bottlenecks — and every
intermediate output is kept, not just the last one.
Concat[ half₀, half₁, b₁, … b_n ] → Conv1×1 → c_out
so the fusion convolution sees 2 + n branches, where C3
sees 2 — more gradient paths at the same channel width.
example, module 4: c = 64, n = 2, Conv1×1 fuses 256 → 128 ch
verified against the reference
All 17 parameterised modules match
yolov8s_cholec80.pt exactly at nc = 7:
That checkpoint needs ultralytics to
unpickle, so its weights are not reused —
training here starts from scratch.
two detection classes
tool — annotated bounding box
tip — 32 × 32 px box on the tip
32 px is the default because a tip box must
hold more anchor points than the assigner's
topk = 10; at 16 px the median is only 4.

g.text: There is no objectness branch and there
are no anchor boxes — see the panels below.

svg.text: What makes it YOLOv8 and not YOLOv5
the head predicts a distribution instead of an offset, and the labels are assigned dynamically
Detect — anchor-free head with Distribution Focal Loss
box branch (hidden 64 ch)
Conv3×3 → Conv3×3 → Conv1×1
out: 4 sides × 16 bins = 64 logits
l, t, r, b — distances from the anchor point
class branch (hidden 128 ch)
Conv3×3 → Conv3×3 → Conv1×1
out: 2 logits — tool, tip
the class score *is* the confidence; there is
no objectness term to multiply in
DFL — turning 16 logits per side into one distance
distance = Σᵢ i · softmax(logits)ᵢ — i = 0 … 15, in grid units
box = dist2bbox( distance, anchor point ) × stride
anchor point = cell centre + 0.5 — a point, not a box. Nothing in the model depends on
a prior box shape, so there are no anchors to tune for this dataset.
Predicting a distribution rather than a single number lets the head express uncertainty about a
blurred or occluded edge: the softmax spreads out instead of committing to one wrong distance.
Li et al., "Generalized Focal Loss", NeurIPS 2020
8400 = 80² + 40² + 20² anchor points per image at 640 × 640
TaskAlignedAssigner — dynamic label assignment
alignment = class score ^ 0.5 × CIoU ^ 6
candidates — anchor points whose centre falls inside the ground-truth box
positives — the topk = 10 best-aligned candidates of each box
conflicts — an anchor claimed by several boxes goes to the one it overlaps most
target — the rescaled alignment becomes the *soft* class target, not 0/1
Which predictions are positive is therefore decided by how well the model is currently doing,
not by the shape of the box — the opposite of YOLOv5's ≤ 4× anchor-ratio matching.
Loss = 7.5 · L_box + 0.5 · L_cls + 1.5 · L_dfl
L_box = 1 − CIoU
L_cls = BCE against the alignment score (not against 0/1)
L_dfl = cross-entropy toward the two bins bracketing the true distance
No objectness term appears anywhere in the loss.
Implementation note: the loss runs in fp32 even under AMP. In half precision the CIoU box-area products
overflow (a 640 px box has area 4 × 10⁵ against a 65504 ceiling) and the whole loss goes NaN within ~20 steps.

Architecture: Ultralytics YOLOv8 · reference checkpoint: cesaraha/yolov8s-surgical-instrument-detection-cholec80 · assignment: Feng et al., "TOOD", ICCV 2021 — this is an independent reimplementation, not a fork.
